page: Amazon Web Services m5.4xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8175M processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz. The instance provides 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, translating to 4.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage or GPU accelerators are bundled with this instance type, and it features a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate a clear performance profile. Single-core processing capabilities, including stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores, fall into the weak category, representing the bottom 25% of tested hardware. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, placing in the middle 50% across stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth for both cached and uncached operations remains in the average tier, with uncached read speeds reaching 87.77 GB/sec and write speeds at 45.25 GB/sec.

Given its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the m5.4xlarge is designed for general-purpose workloads. It demonstrates average performance in database operations, Redis SET operations at 13.15 million operations per second, and static web serving at 11.92 GB/sec. It is also capable of handling software compilation and small-scale language model inference, though its weak single-core performance and lack of local storage or GPU acceleration make it less suitable for high-performance computing or large-scale deep learning. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, it offers a stable, dedicated resource profile for standard enterprise applications, web servers, and development environments that require balanced compute and memory without extreme single-threaded performance demands.
